# Content audit — does the disk match the label?

<!-- generated -->
*Generated by `uv run tools/audit_contents.py`. Do not edit — the next build overwrites it.*

144 items. **6 have been checked against their pages**; the rest carry metadata inherited from RISM, a portal search page, or a filename.

Nothing here proves an item is wrong. These are disagreements between what an item says and what is on disk, ranked so that looking goes where it pays. Read one with

```sh
uv run boc.py look digitizations/<folder>
```

which stacks the top of every page into one column — quartet headings, part names and tempo marks all line up and the structure reads in a glance.

## The flags

| flag | means | learned from |
|---|---|---|
| `span-shared` | another folder claims the same Gérard span and is a very different size | Op. 58: two livraisons both labelled G 242–247, each actually holding three quartets |
| `thin` | very few pages for the works claimed — usually one part-book, not the set | `btv1b108778048`, 15 pages for six quartets |
| `count-mismatch` | the folder spans more works than the item has Gérard numbers for | RISM gives a six-quartet print one number |
| `parts-short` | a part-set with fewer than four part files | the Boyer Op. 9, V2 and VC only |
| `ocr-disagrees` | the print's own headings do not match its label — see the last column | Op. 58, two works per part-book against three declared |

The reading lives in `../structure/<scan-id>.json`: what was seen, on which page, and what RISM says for comparison. It is machine output and regenerable — correct it by recording `contents_verified` in the item's `metadata.json`, or, when the fact belongs to the RISM record rather than to our copy, in `../corrections.json`. Both outrank the reading.
